$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-08 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report ddb5b13e. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v36 index for sub2api (INDEX 980ffdc2) built by publish-tee-images run 34203972720 from commit 98af36197; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin because deploy/attestor carries no change since that release, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones (RTMR3 event log and control plane). The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release ships the OpenAI/ChatGPT side of the two-sided market: contributors can now share a ChatGPT (Codex) subscription through OAuth alongside the existing Claude supply, earning the same 50% revenue share; consumer billing for OpenAI usage is a separate multiplier from Claude. Backend additions are confined to the supply/contributor and OpenAI subsystems - a platform-parameterized onboarding/reauth path with an OpenAI OAuth provider, per-platform probe and settlement (share ratio by platform, health by platform), an OpenAI gateway supply-overflow wrapper, and a supply-pool settings shape that went from a single Claude pair to multiple pairs keyed by platform while remaining byte-identical for the existing Claude pair. The Claude consumer serving path is untouched: no change to the Anthropic relay/forward core, the client fingerprint, the impersonated client-version constant, or the scheduler. It adds one schema migration, 239, which adds a pool_key column to supply_overflow_daily (default 'anthropic', existing rows backfilled) and widens that table's primary key from (day) to (day, pool_key); it coexists with the fork's other migrations because the runner keys applied migrations by filename, not numeric prefix. The whole change was verified before rollout: full backend build and vet, the entire backend unit suite (51 packages), the supplier integration suite, frontend type-check build and unit tests including the i18n parity checks, and a full-startup rehearsal of migration 239 against a restored copy of the production database in which the migration applied in interleaved order and the application initialized and served health with no panic. A full postgres backup was taken and verified immediately beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 110 COPY sections - and it is the rollback point for the schema change. Note that at rollout there is no OpenAI account or OpenAI group configured in production yet, so consumer GPT-6 serving is not live until an account is attached; the frontend advertises the contributor ChatGPT-sharing feature (which this release enables) but does not yet claim live consumer GPT-6 availability. Earlier in this line: proof-v35 (large upstream sync to 0.2.1 plus GPT-6 Astra), proof-v34 (fingerprint version floor), proof-v33 (raise the built-in impersonated client version), proof-v32 (two distinct experiences for consumer and contributor), proof-v31 (a data migration), v29, v28, v27, v26 (earlier upstream sync, Claude Fable 5.1), v24..v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. This rollout completed in 85 seconds with no incident.
